facts_ai_relies_on: A one-line verdict first: every ChatGPT answer opened with a direct yes or a headline range ('Yes, UK citizens can legally get married in Portugal'; '100 guests typically costs around EUR 25,000 to 45,000').

Lead time: 'organise the marriage process at least 1 month before the date' (justica.gov.pt) appeared in all three legal answers; processing 'at least four weeks' and a 6-month window after authorisation (3 months per the AU Embassy, conflicting).
No residency needed: stated in the AU, US and UK answers.
Documents list by passport: passport, birth certificate (recent, translated, apostille where needed), proof of freedom to marry (CNI or equivalent), divorce or death certificate if relevant.
Recognition at home: AU, US and UK answers each ended the legal section with whether the marriage is recognised at home.
Symbolic alternative: 'legally marry at home and have a symbolic ceremony' offered in the Sintra and Algarve answers.

Cost by guest count with a named source and year: UK AIO quotes ritaplacidophotography.com 'EUR 25,000 to EUR 70,000 for 100 guests'; US AIO and ChatGPT use guest bands (under 30, about 50, 80+) and regional ranges; ChatGPT cited only 2026-dated cost pages.
Cost line items as a table: venue, food and drinks per guest, planner, photography, flowers, music, contingency.

Regions as a short list with a fixed attribute set: best for, airport (Faro, Lisbon, Porto), style, main consideration. Entities used: Algarve, Lisbon, Sintra (and Cascais), Douro Valley, Alentejo; Madeira offered as an option in the UK legal answer.
Months as a table: May to June, September (favourite), early October, July to August hot and peak-priced.

Named venues with capacities and transfer times: Forte da Cruz up to 200, Monserrate up to 72, Casa dos Penedos up to 220, castle venues 20 to 40 minutes from Lisbon Airport (US AIO 'castle wedding portugal').
Palace rules: Monserrate and Pena via Parques de Sintra (Pena restricted). No answer mentioned that Queluz and the National Palace of Sintra can be withdrawn for state events.

Planner selection criteria: full service vs day-of coordination, fee separate from the wedding budget, ask for a written fee proposal with VAT; third-party listings (thewed.com, weddingsonline.ie reviews, aisle.wedding profiles) used as proof.

Closing pattern: ChatGPT ended 6 of 7 answers by asking region, guest count, budget and legal or symbolic ceremony; the 14 Oct UK AIO did the same (research doc s8). This mirrors the planned B3 form fields.

content_requirements: S1 QUICK ANSWER, first two sentences under the H1 (plain text, not an image or accordion): 'You can have a wedding in Portugal without living there: there is no residency rule, and the civil marriage process must be organised at least one month before your date.' Source: justica.gov.pt (research doc s5, all couples); pt.usembassy.gov ('residence is not required'). Proposed fact GEO-P01. Follow it with one line: 'Many couples hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home.' (research doc s4 row 1).

S5 'Marrying legally' TAB: one sentence per passport, each starting with the passport name in bold, in this order: AU, US, UK. AU (hedged until research doc q1 is answered): 'Australian passport: Portugal may ask you to prove you are free to marry, usually with a Certificate of No Impediment (CNI). DFAT can issue one in Australia, but check with the Portuguese registry where it must be issued and whether it needs an apostille.' (smartraveller.gov.au; GEO-P02, unconfirmed). US: 'US passport: the US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a certificate of no impediment, so you sign a statement of eligibility to marry before a consular officer. Allow at least four weeks for processing and marry within six months of approval.' (pt.usembassy.gov, confirmed by curl 15 Oct; GEO-P03). UK (hedged until research doc q2 is answered): 'UK passport: Portugal may ask for proof you are free to marry, such as a CNI, which you apply for through the FCDO online service with a valid British passport.' (gov.uk; GEO-P04, unconfirmed). Never apply the US four-week and six-month lines to AU or UK couples.

S5 'Marrying legally' TAB, directly after the passport lines: one recognition line per market that the research doc sources. AU: 'An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is recognised if it was valid in Portugal and is valid under Australian law.' (smartraveller.gov.au; GEO-P05). AI answers close the legal section with recognition. Add US and UK recognition lines only once the fact-checker sources them.

S5 'Marrying legally' TAB format: a numbered 4-step list (choose your town and contact its Registo Civil; gather documents for your passport; submit the process at least one month ahead; hold the ceremony and collect the certificate). Name the Registo Civil and the CNI in full on first mention. Link 'See the full rules by passport' to /destinations/legal-requirements/portugal when it goes live (F007). Replace the live '3 to 6 months' and one-size document list, which have no source (F015).

S2 REGION CHOOSER: 5 cards using AI entity names as card titles: 'Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais', 'The Algarve', 'Porto and the Douro Valley', 'Comporta and the Alentejo', 'Madeira'. Each card has the same labelled lines in the same order so the block reads as a list: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests (range). Airports: Lisbon (LIS), Faro (FAO), Porto (OPO), Madeira (FNC) (research doc s4). Comporta and the Alentejo: leave the airport line as LIS with no drive time until it is sourced (the live 'an hour south of Lisbon' has no source). Sourced travel lines allowed: 'Most Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the centre' (lisbonweddingplanner.com FAQ) and 'The Douro is about 3 hours north of Lisbon' (The Knot, 2024). Proposed facts GEO-P06, GEO-P07. Guest ranges need a source or the fact-checker's sign-off; leave them blank otherwise.

S2 SINTRA CARD palace strip, 3 lines directly under the card: 'Monserrate, Pena, Queluz, the National Palace of Sintra and the Portuguese School of Equestrian Art can be hired for private events through Parques de Sintra. Queluz and the National Palace of Sintra can be withdrawn for state events, and nothing may be fixed to the heritage.' (parquesdesintra.pt, curl 15 Oct; GEO-P08). This is the only palace fact no AI answer carries, so state it plainly and close to the 'Sintra palace' FAQ.

S5 COSTS TAB as an HTML table with columns Item | Range (EUR) | Source and date, for about 100 guests: Total EUR 25,000 to 70,000; Planner EUR 2,000 to 10,000; Venue EUR 3,000 to 15,000+; Catering EUR 80 to 200 per person; Photography EUR 1,500 to 6,000; Civil paperwork and translations EUR 200 to 500. Source: ritaplacidophotography.com, February 2025 (research doc s5; GEO-P09). The UK AI Overview already quotes this exact EUR 25,000 to 70,000 range, so matching it makes the page a corroborating citation. Under the table add: 'Real-wedding venue spend ranged from USD 12,000 (2 nights, sleeps 70, north) to USD 77,000 (3 nights, sleeps about 40, high season).' (kaynorthrupevents.com, June 2025; GEO-P10). Add a caption: 'Ranges in euros; AUD, USD and GBP amounts vary with the exchange rate. Checked October 2026.' No WW figure and no 'From AUD' price. Do not add the under-30 and 50-to-80 guest bands until everafterframes.com is verified (research doc s5). Delete the live 'EUR 120 to 220 per guest' and 'EUR 4,000 to 8,000 planner' figures, which have no source (F015).

S4 or COSTS TAB 'Know how Portuguese venues charge' box, 4 short lines, no prices: exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee; fees may be charged per day or per guest with a minimum; venue fees may be quoted before 23% VAT. (helloportugalconcepts.com, 2024; research doc s2 and s5; GEO-P11). This matches the 'ask for a written proposal with VAT' advice the planner answer gives.

S5 'When to go' TAB as a 3-row table (Season | What to expect): Spring (best months, mild); Summer (hot, peak prices); Autumn (best months, Douro harvest in September). Add a note that Sintra has a cooler microclimate. Source: The Knot, 2024 (research doc s5; GEO-P12). AI answers present months as a table; do not add month-level claims beyond these.

S2 ALGARVE CARD plus FAQ 'Can you have a beach wedding in Portugal?': first sentence 'Yes, but all beaches in Portugal are public, and beach weddings such as in the Algarve need extra permits.' (lisbonweddingplanner.com FAQ; The Knot 2024; GEO-P13).
